sections.label: Consolidated gambling tax administration
sections.summary: The Bill harmonises tax administration, enforcement powers and penalties for gambling duties with other IRAS-administered tax Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The consolidated Act will provide for common tax administration, enforcement powers and penalties across the duties on betting and sweepstakes and private lotteries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The last significant BSDA amendments made were in 2005 but relating to duties and not enforcement or administration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, this Bill harmonises the tax administration and enforcement provisions between the BSDA and the PLA and aligns the tax administration and enforcement for the gambling duties, with other tax Acts administered by IRAS.

sections.label: Non-filing fine alignment
sections.summary: The Bill proposes a fine of up to $5,000 for non-filing of gambling duty returns, aligned with the Income Tax and GST Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The same offence in the Income Tax Act and GST Act attracts a fine of up to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This Bill proposes that, for gambling duties, the fine for non-filing of returns will be up to $5,000, aligned with the Income Tax Act and GST Act.

sections.label: Premium gaming tax rates
sections.summary: For premium gaming, the first $2.4 billion of annual gross gaming revenue is taxed at 8% and the rest at 12%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For premium gaming, the first $2.4 billion of gross gaming revenue per year will be taxed at 8% and the rest at 12%.

sections.label: Gambling social costs and levies
sections.summary: The passage notes less visible social costs of expanded gambling and that higher casino entry levies cut citizen and PR visits to 2.7% in FY2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, while there may be visible economic benefits from the investment and expansion of the two new Integrated Resorts (IRs), we should always bear in mind the less visible social costs and risks of negative externalities associated with an expanded gambling scene in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I recognise that casino entry levies have been raised in 2019, and this has resulted in visits made by Singapore Citizens and PRs falling to 2.7% of the adult population in FY2019 from 4% in FY2018.

sections.label: FY2019 betting tax revenue
sections.summary: Betting taxes for FY2019, before COVID-19, accounted for $2.6 billion in Government revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In absolute terms, I note that betting taxes for FY2019, which is prior to the onset of COVID-19, account for $2.6 billion in Government revenues.

sections.label: FY2021 betting tax estimate
sections.summary: The Government estimated betting taxes would increase by 30.4% to $2.4 billion in FY2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the Budget Statement last year, the Government shared that betting taxes are estimated to increase by a significant 30.4% to $2.4 billion in FY2021.

sections.label: Tiered casino tax rates
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can share its considerations behind the tiered casino tax rates of 8% and 12% for premium gaming and 18% and 22% for mass gaming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As such, I believe the Government would, presumably, have conducted a comprehensive assessment as to the effect of the higher casino tax rates, as this rate cannot be changed in the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, a second related question is whether the Government can share its key considerations and deliberations before finally arriving at the current tiered casino tax rates of 8% and 12% of the gross gaming revenue (GGR) for premium gaming and 18% and 22% for mass gaming respectively.

sections.label: Integrated resorts cumulative EBITDA
sections.summary: The passage estimates that both IRs generated cumulative EBITDA of more than S$30 billion from 2010 to 2020, more than double their $15 billion 2006 investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Fast forward to today, I estimate that both IRs have, over the period from 2010 to 2020, generated a cumulative EBITDA of more than S$30 billion – more than double the $15 billion that they have invested in 2006, and counting.

sections.label: IR expansion delays and exclusivity
sections.summary: The passage states the Government extended casino exclusivity to end 2030, and that both IRs indicated potential delays to their expansion project completions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a reference point using Sands, given that it has operations across Macau, Singapore, as well as Las Vegas, I estimate that, in pre-COVID-19 FY2019, Sands enjoyed the highest EBITDA margins in Singapore at 54%, compared to 36% in Macau and 26% in the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Back in 2019, the Government noted that, in view of the substantial investment of $9 billion by the two IRs and to provide business certainty, the Government had agreed to extend the exclusivity period for the two casinos to end 2030, if no other casinos are to be introduced during this period, Minister Gan Kim Yong shared in a reply to my PQ that the IRs remain committed to delivering on their expansion plans, but both have indicated that there will be potential delays in the completion of their projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That much is clear, given Sands has shared that they may not be able to meet the target 2025 completion deadline they had previously indicated, even though completion was only required by April 2027; while Genting Singapore had announced in early 2021 that it would delay development of its RWS 2.0 expansion project until 2022.

sections.label: Remission of gambling duties
sections.summary: The new section 12(1) provides for remission of gambling duties when the gambling duties are incompatible with the purposes of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 12(1) provides for the remission of gambling duties when the gambling duties are incompatible with the purposes of the Act.

sections.label: Limit on penalty tax
sections.summary: The new section 14(2) limits the amount of penalty tax that can be imposed to 50% of the amount of gambling duties outstanding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 14(2) limits the amount of penalty tax that can be imposed to 50% of the amount of gambling duties outstanding.

sections.label: Court of Appeal gambling cases
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's public policy on gambling has been scrutinised in Court of Appeal cases, including Liao Eng Kiat vs Burswood Nominees Ltd and Poh Soon Kiat vs Desert Palace Incorporated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The position of Singapore's public policy on gambling has been scrutinised in a series of Court of Appeal cases, including Liao Eng Kiat vs Burswood Nominees Ltd and Poh Soon Kiat vs Desert Palace Incorporated.

sections.label: IRAS projected revenue from Bill
sections.summary: A Member asks how much more revenue IRAS projects to earn after the Bill is implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, how much more revenue does IRAS project to earn, following the implementation of the Bill?

sections.label: IRs 2019 investment commitment
sections.summary: In 2019 the two IRs committed around S$9 billion in investments to build new tourism and MICE facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In 2019, the two IRs committed around S$9 billion in investments to build new world-class tourism and MICE facilities.

sections.label: IR expansions economic contribution
sections.summary: The IRs' expansions are expected to contribute S$500 million annually to GDP and create up to 5,000 new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: To Mr Gan Thiam Poh's question on the potential increase in economic contribution, based on our initial projections, the IRs' expansions are expected to contribute S$500 million annually to GDP in a steady state.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The expansions will also create up to 5,000 new jobs directly and benefit local businesses, especially in the construction and services sector.

sections.label: Additional gaming machines and AGA
sections.summary: The IRs may have additional gaming machines and buy additional Approved Gaming Area, with AGA share of floor area falling from 3.2% to 2.4%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For the new attractions and facilities in the expanded IRs to remain commercially viable, the Government also announced in April 2019 that the IRs would be allowed to have additional gaming machines and the option to purchase additional Approved Gaming Area, or AGA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: However, even if the IRs fully utilised their options, AGA, as a proportion of total floor area, would be reduced from 3.2% to 2.4%.

sections.label: IRAS cost of collection
sections.summary: In fiscal year 2020 IRAS kept its cost of collection at less than one cent per dollar of tax revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In fact, fiscal year 2020, across all taxes, IRAS has kept its cost of collection low, at less than one cent for every dollar of tax revenue collected.

sections.label: Taxpayer data confidentiality for gambling duties
sections.summary: Clause 43 ensures taxpayer data collected by IRAS for gambling duties is regarded as secret and confidential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Clause 43 of the Bill ensures that all taxpayer data collected by IRAS for the gambling duties will be regarded as secret and confidential.

sections.label: Betting taxes and sweepstakes
sections.summary: The changes affect only betting operators and private lottery promoters, not retailers, and raising betting taxes is not contemplated in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The changes only affect the betting operator or the private lottery promoter, rather than retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Louis Chua asked if the Government would consider a raising of betting taxes, particularly with regard to sweepstakes and private lotteries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: These are not being contemplated as part of this Bill.

sections.label: Casino and betting tax revenue
sections.summary: With only two casinos, the Government cannot disclose casino tax revenue or its breakdown; total betting taxes were $2.6 billion in FY2019 and $1.8 billion in FY2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As there are only two casinos in Singapore, the Government is unable to disclose the amount of casino tax revenue or the breakdown between premium and mass gaming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The total revenue from all betting taxes was $2.6 billion in FY2019 and $1.8 billion in FY2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The numbers are still being finalised for FY2021 but we do not expect them to recover to pre-COVID-19 levels in the short term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The increase in tax revenue would depend on how well the IRs do after their additional investments.

sections.label: MICE pilots and IR expansions
sections.summary: Four MICE pilots were undertaken last year and went well, and IR expansions are necessary to position the IRs as a tourism enabler.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Last year, we were preparing the tourism and MICE sectors for such an eventuality and, so, we undertook four MICE pilots and those pilots went well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: With regard to the IR expansions, these are also necessary, as the Member noted earlier, to put the IRs in a good position as a tourism enabler for Singapore in the long run.

sections.label: Concern over illegal space
sections.summary: The concern is not about the regulated space but over the illegal space, while being prepared to take the uplift.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And we must be prepared to take that uplift and we must be prepared to carry that wind when it comes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: However, our concern is not about the regulated space but over the illegal space.

sections.label: Safeguards and problem gambling monitoring
sections.summary: A fuller exposition on safeguards is worth a separate airing as it involves various agencies including MHA, but the Government closely monitors problem gambling including online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think a fuller exposition on all the safeguards that the relevant authorities have put into this is probably worth a separate airing, not related to this Bill, because this comes under various agencies, including MHA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But I would assure the Member that the Government pays close attention to this and we continue to keep a close watch to monitor the issue of problem gambling, including problem gambling online.      .
